info.title: Presence API
info.description:
Shows who else has a resource open in an epilot builder, such as a journey, a portal or a flow,
and whether they are viewing it or editing it.

Presence is short-lived: a session counts as present for `ttl_seconds` after its last heartbeat
and is then discarded. No history of who was present is kept.

There is no read-only operation. Seeing who is on a resource means announcing yourself there,
so nobody can see colleagues without being seen.

tags.name: Presence
tags.description: Who else has a resource open

post.description:
Announces the caller on a resource, or refreshes their presence there, and returns everyone
currently present.

Send a heartbeat when the resource is opened, every `heartbeat_interval_seconds` while it stays
open, and right away when the state changes between `viewing` and `editing`.

Requires view permission on the resource itself (see `resource_type`). The caller is always
identified by the access token.

200.description: Everyone currently present on the resource, including the caller.

post.description:
Removes the caller's session from the resource at once, for example when the tab closes or the
user navigates away.

A reload that heartbeats again within a few seconds keeps the user's place in the member order.
Leaving is best effort: a session that never leaves is discarded after `ttl_seconds` anyway.

204.description: The session has left the resource, or was already gone.

OrgId.name: x-epilot-org-id
OrgId.description:
Organization that owns the resource, when the resource is shared with the caller's organization
(for example a flow shared with a partner). Permissions are then checked in that organization.

EpilotAuth.description: Authorization header with epilot OAuth2 bearer token

BadRequest.description: The request is invalid, for example an unknown resource type or a malformed session id.

Unauthorized.description: The access token is missing or invalid.

Forbidden.description: The caller has no view permission on the resource, or the token does not identify a user.

PresenceResourceType.description:
Kind of resource, and the permission needed to see who is present on it:
- `journey`: `entity:view` on the journey. The resource ID is the journey's entity ID.
- `customer_portal`: `customer_portal:view` on the portal
- `installer_portal`: `installer_portal:view` on the portal
- `flow`: `workflow:definition:view` on the flow

PresenceState.description: `viewing`: the resource is open. `editing`: it is open with unsaved changes.

SessionId.description: Generated by the client, one per browser tab. A user can be present with several tabs.

InstanceId.description:
Optional. Generated by the client each time it starts sending heartbeats in a tab. A leave that
carries it only takes effect while that instance sent the session's latest heartbeat, so a late
leave from an earlier instance in the same tab cannot remove the session.

PresenceMember.description: A user present on the resource. Several tabs of the same user count as one member.

user_id.description: epilot user ID. Names and avatars come from the User API.

user_org.description: Organization of the user. On a shared resource it can differ from the owning organization.

last_seen_at.description: Time of the user's latest heartbeat on the resource.

members.description:
Everyone present, in order of arrival. The order stays stable between heartbeats. On a
shared resource, a partner organization sees the owning organization's users and its own.

ttl_seconds.description: Seconds after its last heartbeat that a session stops counting as present.

heartbeat_interval_seconds.description: How often clients should send a heartbeat, in seconds.

truncated.description: True when more users are present than one response lists; `members` is then incomplete.

error.description: Error message, or the list of validation errors for a 400.
